name: C2PA: Content Credentials Standards for AI Provenance in Media
title: C2PA: Content Credentials Standards for AI Provenance in Media
answer: C2PA is an open technical standards body, a Joint Development Foundation project, that publishes Content Credentials, a cryptographically signed provenance standard for images, video, audio and documents. Its site explains how the standard labels synthetic and non-synthetic content, including the IPTC digitalSourceType field, the c2pa.ai-disclosure assertion, Regions of Interest, inputTo ingredient assertions and Actions. It also reports adoption by Amazon, Meta, OpenAI, TikTok and others. For media readers, the most useful item is the white paper and deployment guidance on attaching and verifying provenance for AI-generated or AI-modified assets.

sections.body: C2PA publishes c2pa.org. C2PA describes itself as an open, technical standards body addressing misleading information online through technical standards for certifying source and history of digital content, and as a Joint Development Foundation project. The site carries news announcements, an FAQ, a white paper titled 'Use of Content Credentials to Identify Synthetic and Non-Synthetic Content', and a companion 'Content Credentials Deployment Guidance'. Its scope is content provenance and the Content Credentials standard, including synthetic and non-synthetic labeling, conformance, certificates, metadata interoperability, durable credentials and offline workflows. The pages read include announcements dated to July 27, 2026, and an event held on October 2, 2024. The site was read on October 1, 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: C2PA publishes and maintains Content Credentials, a digital standard that provides information about how and when digital content was created or modified. Credentials are tamper-evident, cryptographically signed data structures that travel with an asset. Each credential is digitally signed by a trusted implementation and includes cryptographic hashes of both the asset and the provenance data. Any modification, intentional or accidental, breaks the cryptographic linkage and signals tampering. The white paper explains how developers, creators and platforms can use Content Credentials to communicate provenance. It focuses on labeling AI-generated, AI-modified and non-synthetic content. The IPTC digitalSourceType field is the primary signal for declaring whether an asset was generated by a model, enhanced by AI, captured by a device, or edited by a human. A new c2pa.ai-disclosure assertion captures model provenance, scientific domain and the degree of human oversight. Regions of Interest identify which portions of an asset were affected by AI, such as an image region, document paragraphs, or audio and video segments. inputTo ingredient assertions can record prompts, reference images, seed values and parameters behind a generation. The Actions assertion records each step in an asset's lifecycle using terms such as c2pa.created, c2pa.opened and c2pa.edited. An AI usage indicator can be applied to each action, so a single file can distinguish a human-created original from a subsequent AI-assisted edit. The companion deployment guidance is a practical, non-technical overview for businesses, agencies, publishers and governments on adopting Content Credentials and verifying provenance for audiences.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: C2PA says it has more than 500 members and over 6,000 affiliates supporting the standard. Andrew Jenks, Executive Chair, described Content Credentials as the work product of over 200 global member organizations. C2PA was created in 2020, and in April 2023 it released version 1.3 of its technical specification, with expanded support for media types and generative AI transparency. The specification was being examined by ISO's TC 171/SC 2 committee and was expected to become a global standard in early 2025. TikTok said it has labeled over 3 billion pieces of content as AI-generated through Content Credentials, invisible watermarking, creator education and labeling tools. The Publicis announcement says Publicis Groupe is present in over 100 countries and employs around 90,000 professionals. Amazon said all Amazon Titan-generated images contain an invisible watermark by default. C2PA defines Content Credentials as a digital nutrition label for media, and content provenance as the recorded history of a piece of digital content from creation through subsequent modifications or uses.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in Media, this source is the standards body's own account of how provenance is being standardised through an open specification. It gives newsrooms the vocabulary and mechanisms to attach to synthetic assets, including digitalSourceType, c2pa.ai-disclosure, Regions of Interest, inputTo and Actions. It also shows where the standard is being implemented in tools that reach media workflows, such as Amazon Titan Image Generator and AWS Elemental MediaConvert for broadcast and multi-screen delivery, and in platform labeling by Meta and TikTok. The deployment guidance speaks directly to publishers and agencies about choosing tools that preserve credentials by default and verifying provenance for audiences. That makes it useful for planning how to label, verify and distribute AI-generated or AI-modified media.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: This is C2PA's own site, so it presents the standard and its adoption from the organisation's perspective. The pages read are news announcements, an FAQ and guidance rather than the full technical specification. They do not offer independent testing of whether credentials survive common newsroom workflows, nor editorial or legal advice. Some claims are forward-looking, such as OpenAI's plan to attach Content Credentials to Sora video when the model is ready for public deployment, and ISO approval expected in early 2025, and the pages read do not confirm those outcomes. The site also does not cover pricing, implementation costs or competing provenance standards.
